children: The Indian rupee trimmed early gains to trade nearly flat on Tuesday as oil prices rebounded from a more-than-two-week on reports of fresh US strikes on Iran amid heightened focus on diplomacy in the Middle East and a key election in the US.
was at 94.87 per dollar, nearly flat on day after touching a 10-day high of 94.62 in early trading.

Oil prices edged higher on Tuesday after a report that the United States had struck Iran's Qeshm Island, raising fears of an escalation in the eight-month conflict and prolonged disruptions to Middle East oil supplies.
The strikes came after hopes surrounding diplomatic efforts to end the war had pushed down Brent crude prices by about 11% in the previous session. Brent prices were last up 2% at $107 per barrel.
Iran and the United States are far from reaching a deal to end the war, a senior Iranian official told Reuters on Tuesday, adding that Tehran would not accept Washington's "excessive demands".
Investor anxiety also remains elevated as Americans head to polls later in the day.

American voters will deliver a verdict on the first two years of President Donald Trump's second term in Tuesday's midterm elections, with polls and nonpartisan analysts favoring Democrats to wrest the House from Republicans while control of the Senate remains uncertain.
The outcome of the elections are expected to hold implications for a wide range of policies including around the AI sector and the likely trajectory of the Iran war going forward.
With the focus on global cues, traders in the Indian FX market steered clear of outsized positioning and took their cues from moves in oil prices.

"We are forecasting USD/INR at 96.000 by December 2026 and 97.500 by September 2027, implying a gradual depreciation in INR against the US dollar and a modest underperformance against other Asian currencies," analysts at MUFG said in a note.
